# The knowledge base

A tree of folders and .json files with facts for agents. Two tools: `knowledge_read` looks things up (read, ls, find); `knowledge_write` changes a knowledge base of your own (add, set, rm).

- How to look things up: `aos/knowledge.json#/read`.
- Which knowledge base you may write: `aos/knowledge.json#/where`.
- When to write, and the calls: `aos/knowledge.json#/write`.
- Size, the index, no lock: `aos/knowledge.json#/rules`.

read._description: Tool knowledge_read: read, ls and find; the root you got at the start or one you give; paths; errors.

where._description: Which knowledge base you may write: root in the call or AOS_KNOWLEDGE; never the stock one.

write._description: Tool knowledge_write: when to write, and the add, set and rm calls.

rules._description: add without value, suggested sizes, the index, no lock, and the write errors.

read:
# Looking things up: knowledge_read

The knowledge base is a tree: folders, .json files, and keys inside them. At the start you got its root (its index, one line per child); that root is what `knowledge_read` reads. You do not need to know where it is on disk.

- The root again: `{"op": "read"}`.
- One place: `{"op": "read", "path": "aos/errors.json#/codes"}`. A path is folder/file.json#/key/subkey; keep `.json`. Copy paths exactly as read, ls and find print them. Do not start a path with `/` (that is a file system path).
- Another knowledge base (for example one you wrote with `knowledge_write`): add the same `"root": "my-notes"` you gave there, e.g. `{"op": "read", "path": "notes/amy.json", "root": "my-notes"}`.
- Only the children: `{"op": "ls", "path": "aos/cli/"}`.
- Search: `{"op": "find", "query": "timeout"}` (names, descriptions and text, any case; `tag` = an exact tag). A hit inside a text shows its line as `[match: ...]`: read the hit whose line answers you.
- Long output stops at `max_bytes` (default 8000) with `[truncated: N more bytes]`: read a deeper path.

Errors: `NodeMissing` (the line lists what is there), `PathBad`, `TargetBad` (ls on a text: use read), `KnowledgeMissing` / `KnowledgeBad` (no usable knowledge base is set up for you and no usable root given: say so).
where:
# Which knowledge base you write

- The knowledge base you read (the root you got at the start, with `aos/` in it) is the stock one. Read it; do not write it. Humans own it.
- Writing needs a knowledge base of your own. Give `root` in the `knowledge_write` call (an existing folder you may write, relative to your workspace), or have `AOS_KNOWLEDGE` set up for that tool. `knowledge_write` has no default.
- `KnowledgeMissing` from `knowledge_write`: you have no knowledge base to write. Give `root`, or tell a human. Do not write into the stock one instead.
- `KnowledgeBad`: `root` (or the one set up for you) is not a folder. Make it first with `mkdir`.
- Read back what you wrote: `knowledge_read` with the same `root`.
- `knowledge_write` not registered: ask a human to register `lib/agent/knowledge_write` (knowledge pack), or add it with `self_tools` (`aos/me.json#/self_tools`). A fixed knowledge base = register it with `AOS_KNOWLEDGE` in its envs (yours, not the stock one).
write:
# When and how to write: knowledge_write

Save reusable facts, not task progress: a verified procedure, a repeated failure and its fix, a stable fact useful to other agents. No secrets, guesses or conversation logs.

First call `knowledge_read` with `{"op":"find","query":"your topic"}` and read what matches. Update an entry instead of adding a duplicate.

The calls (add `"root":"my-notes"` when nothing is set up for you; see `aos/knowledge.json#/where`):

- a folder first, if it is not listed yet: `{"op":"add","path":"notes/","description":"Notes about people"}`
- add: `{"op":"add","path":"notes/amy.json","value":"Amy likes tea.","description":"Who Amy is"}`. `description` is always required: it is the one line in listings. Plain text is a plain string, not JSON inside a string.
- replace: `{"op":"set","path":"notes/amy.json","value":"Amy likes coffee."}`
- remove: `{"op":"rm","path":"notes/amy.json"}` (a folder that is not empty needs `"recursive":true`)

Rules: `aos/knowledge.json#/rules`.
rules:
# Writing: rules

- add without `value` only puts something that already exists into the index (a file you wrote another way); the content stays: `{"op":"add","path":"notes/bob.md","description":"Who Bob is"}`. Not there = `NodeMissing`; `"create":true` makes it empty.
- Aim for about 1 KB per text and about 8 KB per file; split a larger topic into several keys or files. These are suggestions, not limits. Use a short title, a one-sentence summary, and concrete examples.
- Every op updates the index. Never edit `_index.json` yourself.
- There is no lock. If two agents write the same place at the same time, the later write wins. So before `set`, `read` the path again and change the text you just read.
- Errors: `NodeExists` (it is there already: use `set`), `NodeMissing` (the line says what to add first), `ChildrenExist` (rm of a folder that is not empty: add `"recursive":true`), `ValueBad` (a value that does not fit there: not a string for a file that is not .json). Over 8000 bytes in one call is still written, with a warning line: smaller keys or files are easier to read back, `WriteFailed` (the file system does not let you write there). `KnowledgeMissing`, `KnowledgeBad`: `aos/knowledge.json#/where`.
